paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. In the middle of the darkest day there ever was, God was not absent from His own plan. Jesus cried out, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" (Matthew 27:46), and then He yielded up His spirit (Matthew 27:50). He gave His life on purpose, to rescue people from the dark and bring them home (Mark 10:45).

Now look at what happens the moment He dies. The veil of the temple is torn in two from top to bottom (Matthew 27:51), and the tombs break open (Matthew 27:52). I think that's the passage telling us death is not getting the last word, and that the way to God is opened. Nobody sneaks a message like that past a whole planet, so the ground just SHOUTS it.

And then there's the centurion, a Roman officer who was only there for guard duty. He sees it all and says, "Truly this was the Son of God." (Matthew 27:54). The women are there too, still watching from a distance after following Jesus all the way from Galilee (Matthew 27:55). So here's what it means for you, baker: the One who went into the dark for you is the Son of God, and you can trust Him even on your darkest day. I spent years in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you that being found by Him beats any light switch. This story is NOT over.
